html:
Calicuas is the name the map gives to a people of the Allegheny plateau in what is now central West Virginia in 1492. Little is known about them, and the name does not match any well documented tribe.

In the 1400s this region was home to farming villages of the Monongahela culture to the north and the Fort Ancient culture to the west, along the Ohio valley. In the 1600s the Beaver Wars waged by the Iroquois emptied much of the upper Ohio country, and later the Shawnee and others used it as hunting land.
